nodes.text: Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Germline rare disease variant calling and annotation from WES data — alignment, duplicate marking, HaplotypeCaller, VEP annotation, filtering for rare pathogenic variants | germline short-variant calling from paired-end whole-exome sequencing FASTQ or BAM (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller, VEP annotation with ClinVar/OMIM/HPO cross-referencing) → annotated VCF filtered for rare disease candidate variants

Bulk RNA-seq expression outlier and aberrant splicing analysis for rare disease diagnosis — alignment, quantification, OUTRIDER/FRASER or DROP pipeline to detect genes with aberrant expression or splicing | bulk RNA-seq expression outlier and aberrant splicing analysis from paired-end FASTQ (STAR alignment, quantification, OUTRIDER expression outlier detection, FRASER splicing outlier detection) → ranked expression and splicing outlier calls for rare disease candidate genes

Integrate WES variant calls with RNA-seq expression/splicing outlier evidence to rank candidate disease genes and produce a diagnostic report | integration of germline WES variant calls and RNA-seq expression/splicing outlier evidence for rare disease diagnosis — combine genomic variants with transcriptomic aberrations, cross-reference ClinVar/OMIM/HPO → ranked candidate genes with combined evidence and diagnostic report

Whole-exome sequencing (WES) germline variant calling and annotation for rare disease diagnosis | germline variant calling and functional annotation from whole-exome sequencing FASTQ/BAM (SNVs, indels, SVs, VEP annotation, candidate gene ranking) → annotated VCF and prioritized variant list

RNA-seq processing for rare disease: outlier expression and aberrant splicing detection | transcriptome analysis for rare disease from RNA-seq FASTQ (alignment, quantification, aberrant expression and aberrant splicing outlier detection via OUTRIDER/FRASER) → expression and splicing outlier calls

Integrate WES variants and RNA-seq outliers for multi-omic diagnostic candidate prioritization | integration of DNA germline variant calls and RNA aberrant expression/splicing outlier evidence — intersecting candidate genomic variants with functional RNA dysregulation → prioritized multi-omic diagnostic candidate report

Perturb-seq guide assignment: assign sgRNA identities to single cells from guide-count data (Replogle et al. 2022, Cell 185(14):2559-2575, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013) | CRISPR sgRNA guide-to-cell assignment on Perturb-seq single-cell data (guide UMI count thresholding / mixture-model assignment) → per-cell guide identity call matrix

Perturb-seq hit calling: identify significant perturbation effects from guide-assigned single-cell expression data | perturbation hit calling on guide-assigned Perturb-seq single-cell expression data (per-perturbation differential expression vs non-targeting controls) → significant gene/perturbation hits with effect sizes and adjusted p-values

Perturbation state embedding: scVI / scANVI latent embedding and perturbation-state annotation of the Perturb-seq cells | latent embedding and perturbation-state annotation of Perturb-seq single cells using scVI/scANVI variational autoencoders → integrated latent space, UMAP, and per-cell perturbation-state labels

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

Rare disease germline variant calling, annotation, and prioritization from the patient's WES data (paired-end exome FASTQ or accessions) | germline short-variant calling from paired-end whole-exome FASTQ (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller/DeepVariant) with VEP annotation and rare-disease variant prioritization → annotated, ranked candidate causal variants (VCF + prioritized list)

RNA-seq analysis of the patient's sample for aberrant expression and aberrant splicing outlier detection to support the rare disease diagnosis | bulk RNA-seq alignment and quantification from FASTQ with aberrant expression and aberrant splicing outlier detection (DROP-style) → per-gene expression outliers and splicing outliers supporting variant interpretation

Integrate the prioritized WES variants with the RNA-seq expression/splicing outliers to produce a final ranked list of candidate causal genes for the rare disease workup | integration of prioritized germline variants with transcriptomic outlier evidence (expression, splicing) — multi-omics concordance ranking → final candidate causal gene/variant list with combined evidence

Perturb-seq guide RNA assignment and cell demultiplexing | guide barcode assignment and cell demultiplexing from single-cell Perturb-seq guide capture and gene expression libraries → guide-to-cell assignment table and annotated AnnData

Perturb-seq hit calling and differential perturbation effect scoring vs non-targeting controls | statistical hit calling and differential expression testing across CRISPR target perturbations relative to non-targeting controls → ranked hit list and DEG effect sizes

Perturbation state representation and embedding using scVI / scANVI | deep generative modeling of perturbation states using scVI and scANVI on single-cell CRISPR screen data → latent perturbation embedding space and low-dimensional manifold

Guide assignment for Perturb-seq CRISPR screen: assign sgRNAs to individual cells from guide capture sequencing data, following Replogle et al. 2022 Cell | guide RNA assignment from single-cell Perturb-seq guide capture reads — demultiplex guide-bearing cells, assign guide identities per cell barcode, generate cell-by-guide assignment matrix with QC filtering of multiplet and unassigned cells

Hit calling for Perturb-seq screen: identify perturbations with significant transcriptional effects using guide assignments and single-cell expression data, following Replogle et al. 2022 Cell | perturbation hit calling from Perturb-seq single-cell expression matrix with guide assignments — per-guide differential expression vs non-targeting control, effect-size estimation, multiple-testing correction (FDR), ranked list of significant perturbation hits

Find tumor-reactive T cells in scRNA-seq data by clustering, T cell annotation, and tumor-reactivity scoring | single-cell RNA-seq clustering, cell-type annotation, and T cell subset identification with tumor-reactivity marker analysis from scRNA-seq data (FASTQ or count matrix) → cell clusters, T cell populations, tumor-reactive T cell scores

Predict neoantigens from tumor somatic variants and HLA typing | neoantigen prediction from tumor somatic variants (VCF from WES/WGS variant calling) and HLA typing → ranked list of predicted neoantigens with MHC binding affinity and presentation scores

Predict tumor neoantigens and peptide-MHC binding affinities | neoantigen prediction pipeline integrating somatic variant identification/processing, patient HLA typing, and peptide-MHC binding affinity scoring → ranked list of candidate neoepitopes

Load EPIC/450K IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalisation | methylation array IDAT loading and functional normalisation using minfi (Illumina 450K/EPIC), output normalised beta/M values matrix

Differential methylation analysis using DSS on normalised methylation values | differential methylation analysis on normalised beta/M values or bismark bisulfite coverage using DSS (Beta-binomial model), two-group comparison → differentially methylated positions/regions with FDR

Gene-set enrichment analysis on differentially methylated results using missMethyl | gene-set enrichment analysis on differentially methylated CpG/probe lists using missMethyl (GO/KEGG, accounting for probe bias and gene length), output enriched pathways and gene sets

Find tumor-reactive T cells in my scRNA-seq data | single-cell RNA-seq analysis of T cells — QC, clustering, T cell subset annotation, TCR clonotype expansion analysis, and tumor-reactivity signature scoring (e.g., CXCL13, exhaustion/cytotoxicity markers) → identified tumor-reactive T cell clusters with marker genes and clonality

Predict neoantigens from tumor genomic data | neoantigen prediction from tumor somatic variants — somatic variant calling from tumor/normal WES or WGS, HLA typing, mutant peptide extraction, peptide-MHC class I binding affinity prediction → ranked list of candidate neoantigen peptides

Run Monocle3 graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference on the single-cell AnnData h5ad input, using the specified cluster column (monocle_cluster) and root cell (root_cell); outputs pseudotime-annotated AnnData, per-cell pseudotime CSV, and trajectory plots (PNG). | graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference on a single-cell AnnData object (Monocle3: preprocessing, UMAP reduction, clustering, principal-graph learning, cell ordering from a specified root cell) → per-cell pseudotime values, trajectory-annotated h5ad, CSV table, and trajectory plots

Run scVelo RNA velocity analysis on the same single-cell AnnData h5ad input using the specified velocity_mode; outputs velocity-annotated AnnData, velocity/latent-time CSV, and velocity stream plots (PNG). | RNA velocity estimation on a single-cell AnnData object with spliced/unspliced count layers (scVelo: moment-based normalization, velocity estimation in the specified mode, velocity graph and embedding projection) → per-cell velocity vectors and latent time, velocity-annotated h5ad, CSV table, and stream plots

Run DSS differential methylation analysis on the normalised methylation matrix | differential methylation analysis on a normalised methylation beta-value matrix using DSS → differentially methylated CpG loci (DMPs) and differentially methylated regions (DMRs)

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differentially methylated CpGs/genes | gene-set enrichment analysis on differentially methylated CpGs/genes using missMethyl (GO/KEGG with array probe-number bias correction) → enriched gene sets and pathways

Estimate human PK parameters (clearance, volume of distribution) from preclinical rat, mouse, or dog data via allometric inter-species scaling | allometric inter-species scaling of pharmacokinetic parameters (CL, Vd, t_half) from preclinical animal species (rat/mouse/dog) to predict human PK parameters → human clearance and volume estimates for first-in-human dose projection

Run full mechanistic PBPK simulation with compartmental organ model and organ-specific clearance, including optional renal/hepatic impairment submodels for special population dosing | mechanistic whole-body PBPK simulation with compartmental organ model and organ-specific hepatic/renal clearance, with optional renal and hepatic impairment submodels → plasma and tissue concentration-time profiles for healthy and special (impaired) populations

Run Monte Carlo sampling on the PBPK model to characterize inter-individual PK variability in the virtual population | Monte Carlo population variability sampling on PBPK model parameters (physiological and drug-specific) → virtual population PK distributions, prediction intervals, and variability characterization for dose adjustment

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal data (rat, mouse, or dog) using allometric interspecies scaling for PBPK model parameterization | allometric interspecies scaling of preclinical PK parameters (clearance, volume of distribution, half-life) from rat/mouse/dog to human — power-law scaling with exponent correction → predicted human CL, Vd, t½ for PBPK model input

Full PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance, with optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing | mechanistic whole-body PBPK simulation using multi-compartmental model with organ-specific clearance (hepatic extraction, renal filtration) and optional special-population submodel (renal impairment, hepatic impairment) → plasma concentration-time profile, AUC, Cmax, Tmax for standard and special populations

Monte Carlo sampling for variability characterization of PBPK model predictions across population parameter distributions | Monte Carlo simulation sampling across population PK parameter distributions (body weight, organ volumes, blood flows, clearance variability) to characterize inter-individual variability in PBPK predictions → population PK summary statistics, 5th/95th percentile concentration profiles, variability bands

PBPK Simulation — & Special Populations. Mechanistic PBPK simulation for predicting human pharmacokinetics from preclinical animal data. Step 1: to estimate human PK parameters from rat, mouse, or dog data. Step 2: full PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance (optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing). Step 3: Monte Carlo sampling for variability characterization. Use for: species scaling, IND/NDA PBPK packages, first-in-human dose projection, and special population (renal/hepatic impairment) dose adjustments. Required for regulator

Run RNA-seq differential expression analysis to produce a ranked gene signature | bulk RNA-seq differential expression from FASTQ or count matrix, two-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values (ranked gene signature)

Find drugs with transcriptional signature matching the RNA-seq DE results | drug repurposing via transcriptional signature matching — query a LINCS L1000 / CMap connectivity map or TxGNN with the ranked DE gene signature to retrieve compounds whose perturbation profiles inversely or positively correlate with the disease signature

Run RNA-seq analysis (QC, alignment, quantification, differential expression) on the user's samples to produce a transcriptional signature of up- and down-regulated genes | bulk RNA-seq differential expression from raw FASTQ (QC, alignment, quantification, negative-binomial DE model) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values, yielding an up/down DEG signature

Find drugs whose transcriptional signatures match (or oppose) the RNA-seq DE signature by querying LINCS L1000 / Connectivity Map perturbagen profiles | drug repurposing by transcriptional signature matching: query an up/down differential gene expression signature against LINCS L1000 / Connectivity Map compound perturbation profiles → ranked candidate drugs with connectivity scores

RNA-seq processing and differential expression analysis to obtain transcriptional signature | bulk RNA-seq processing and differential expression analysis to generate ranked differentially expressed gene signatures (log2 fold change and p-values)

Screen drug perturbation databases (e.g., CMap/LINCS L1000) using transcriptional signature to identify candidate drugs | connectivity mapping query matching or inverting a user-supplied transcriptional signature against drug-induced expression profiles in CMap/LINCS → ranked drug candidates

ICH S7A Phase A — CNS safety pharmacology in-silico simulation: motor activity, functional convulsions, seizure liability, autonomic/CNS depressant risk prediction for a compound (SMILES/PK profile). | in-silico CNS safety pharmacology panel — seizure-liability and CNS-depressant prediction from molecular structure and/or PK parameters → CNS risk score with ADME/PK context

ICH S7A Phase B — Cardiovascular safety pharmacology in-silico simulation: hERG inhibition, QT prolongation liability, cardiac ionic current (Nav/Cav) profiling, in-silico cardiotoxicity panel for a compound. | in-silico cardiovascular safety panel — hERG channel block prediction + QT-prolongation liability + cardiac ion-channel (Nav/Cav/Kv) inhibition prediction from SMILES → CV risk score

ICH S7A Phase C — Respiratory safety pharmacology in-silico simulation: respiratory-depressant liability, airway/pulmonary effects prediction, respiratory drive assessment for a compound. | in-silico respiratory safety panel — respiratory-depressant and airway-effect prediction from molecular structure and/or PK → respiratory risk score

ICH S7A Phase D — Integrated core-battery risk synthesis: combine CNS (Phase A), cardiovascular (Phase B) and respiratory (Phase C) in-silico findings into a consolidated safety margin / integrated risk profile against therapeutic PK exposure. | integration of three system-level safety pharmacology results (CNS, CV, respiratory) — per-system margin-over-exposure, integrated hazard flag list, cross-system concordance → consolidated safety profile report

Validate a SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) — check parseability, canonicalisation, and remove invalid entries | SMILES validation and canonicalisation from a text file of SMILES+ID pairs → validated, canonicalised SMILES list with IDs

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated SMILES into scaffolds and R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic decomposition of validated SMILES molecules into core scaffolds and attached R-group fragments → scaffold-R-group fragment database

Run mmpdb to compute property deltas for matched molecular pair fragment swaps | Matched molecular pair analysis using mmpdb on the RECAP-derived fragment database — compute property deltas (e.g. logP, MW, activity) for fragment transformations → MMP rules with property change predictions

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA) score | Scaffold ranking by occurrence frequency, drug-likeness (Lipinski/QED), and synthetic accessibility (SA score) from the MMP-derived novel scaffolds → ranked scaffold list with scores

Phase A: In silico cardiovascular safety panel simulation (cardiac ion channels, QTc prolongation, and hemodynamics) | in silico cardiovascular safety pharmacology simulation assessing cardiac ion channel affinities (hERG, Nav1.5, Cav1.2), action potential duration (CiPA APD90), and hemodynamic parameters (MAP, HR) from compound structure/SMILES -> cardiac liability score and predicted QTc prolongation

Phase B: In silico central nervous system (CNS) liability and neurobehavioral screening | computational CNS safety pharmacology evaluation including blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration modeling, neuro-receptor binding panel profiling (GABA-A, NMDA, 5-HT, dopamine), and seizure/sedation liability prediction -> CNS risk profile

Phase C: In silico respiratory safety pharmacology modeling | predictive respiratory safety pharmacology modeling estimating drug-induced alterations in respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute volume, and bronchoconstriction liability -> respiratory depression risk profile

Phase D: Integrated ICH S7A exposure safety margin and therapeutic index assessment | integrated safety pharmacology exposure-margin calculation linking PBPK-predicted clinical Cmax,unbound to in silico vital organ liabilities (cardiovascular, CNS, respiratory) -> ICH S7A safety margins, NOAEL-equivalent bounds, and regulatory summary report
Validate and standardize SMILES input file (one SMILES and compound ID per line) | chemical structure validation and sanitization of input SMILES strings and identifiers → validated SMILES table
RDKit RECAP decomposition of molecules into scaffolds and R-groups | retrosynthetic fragment decomposition of molecules using RDKit RECAP rules → molecular scaffolds and R-group fragments

mmpdb matched molecular pair indexing and property delta calculation for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair generation and property difference calculation using mmpdb → matched molecular pair transformation database

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness (QED), and synthetic accessibility (SA) score | prioritization and ranking of chemical scaffolds by occurrence frequency, QED drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility score → prioritized scaffold report

Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) | validate and standardize a line-delimited SMILES file (SMILES + compound ID per line) with RDKit parsing and canonicalization → cleaned canonical SMILES table with invalid entries flagged

RDKit RECAP decomposition into scaffold + R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic fragmentation of validated molecules into core scaffolds and R-group substituents (RDKit RECAP) → per-molecule fragment table (scaffold + attachment-point-labelled R-groups)

mmpdb: property deltas for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair indexing of RECAP fragments with mmpdb → fragment-swap transformation rules with computed physicochemical property deltas (e.g., logP, MW, TPSA) per matched pair

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, SA score | apply MMP transformations to generate novel scaffold/R-group combinations and rank them by transformation frequency, drug-likeness (QED), and synthetic accessibility (SA score) → prioritized ranked scaffold list

Validate expression matrix and clinical metadata: check matrix dimensions, sample ID concordance, missing values, outlier detection, and metadata completeness | Input validation and QC of a gene expression matrix (rows=genes, cols=samples) paired with a clinical metadata table — check matrix integrity, sample-name concordance, missing-value summary, and basic distribution diagnostics → validation report

Run limma-voom differential expression analysis: voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes moderation, topTable extraction (logFC, adj.P.Val) | limma-voom differential expression on a normalized gene expression matrix with a design matrix including group + covariates — voom precision-weighting, linear-model fit, empirical-Bayes moderation, topTable extraction → per-gene logFC and adjusted p-values

Run GSVA/ssGSEA gene set enrichment on hallmark MSigDB (50 gene sets) to identify top enriched pathways per group | GSVA/ssGSEA pathway enrichment on a gene expression matrix using MSigDB hallmark gene set collection (50 gene sets) — compute per-sample pathway scores, compare enrichment across groups, rank top enriched pathways → hallmark pathway score matrix and ranked pathway list

Summarize and report top enriched pathways per group from GSVA/ssGSEA results with visualization | Summarize GSVA/ssGSEA pathway scores into a final report — group-wise pathway rankings, enrichment significance, heatmap or bar plot of top pathways → annotated results table and visualization

Validate gene expression matrix and matched clinical metadata (sample concordance, missing values, distributions) | input validation and QC of a pre-computed gene expression matrix with matched clinical/sample metadata — sample-ID concordance, missing-value checks, distribution summaries → validated analysis-ready matrix and metadata table

limma-voom differential expression: voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes, topTable (logFC, adj.P.Val) | differential gene expression on a bulk expression matrix using limma-voom (voom precision-weight transformation, linear model with covariate adjustment, empirical Bayes moderation) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values via topTable

GSVA/ssGSEA gene signature scoring on MSigDB Hallmark (50 gene sets); top enriched pathways per group | gene set enrichment scoring (GSVA and ssGSEA) of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets on a normalized expression matrix → per-sample pathway enrichment scores and ranked top enriched pathways per group
Validate RNA-seq expression matrix and clinical metadata | validation and consistency checking of gene expression matrix and matched clinical metadata tables

Differential expression analysis via limma-voom with linear modeling, covariates, eBayes moderation, and topTable | differential gene expression testing using limma-voom transformation and linear models with covariates → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

Gene signature scoring via GSVA/ssGSEA on MSigDB hallmark gene sets to identify top enriched pathways per group | single-sample gene set variation analysis (GSVA/ssGSEA) on MSigDB hallmark gene sets from normalized expression data → sample-level pathway enrichment scores and group comparisons
